q1.desc: Monthly 30-day retention inputs for each channel, region and signup cohort, January to August 2026
q1.sql:
-- 30-day retention inputs by channel, region and cohort month, Jan to Aug 2026
select
    channel,
    region,
    cohort_month,
    cohort_customers,
    retained_30d
from marts.retention_by_channel
where cohort_month between '2026-01-01' and '2026-08-31'

q2.desc: New customers for each channel who signed up in August 2026
q2.sql:
-- New customers by channel, August 2026
select
    channel,
    signup_month,
    new_customers
from marts.acquisition_by_channel
where signup_month between '2026-08-01' and '2026-08-31'

x1.given: Retention targets by channel for August 2026, shared as a CSV by the growth lead

v1.desc: Retention for each channel and month, with each channel ranked against the others in its month
v1.sql:
-- Monthly 30-day retention by channel, with each channel's rank in its month
select
    channel,
    cohort_month,
    sum(retained_30d) / sum(cohort_customers) as retention,
    rank() over (
        partition by cohort_month
        order by sum(retained_30d) / sum(cohort_customers) desc
    ) as retention_rank
from q1
group by channel, cohort_month

v2.desc: August new customers and retention for each channel, side by side
v2.sql:
-- August new customers and 30-day retention by channel
select
    q2.channel,
    q2.new_customers,
    sum(q1.retained_30d) / sum(q1.cohort_customers) as retention
from q2
join q1
    on q1.channel = q2.channel
    and q1.cohort_month = q2.signup_month
group by q2.channel, q2.new_customers
order by retention desc

f1.desc: Paid social's retention for the August 2026 signup cohort
f1.sql:
select retention
from v1
where channel = 'paid_social'
  and cohort_month = '2026-08-01'
f1.label: Paid social retention, August

f2.desc: Paid social's retention for the July 2026 signup cohort
f2.sql:
select retention
from v1
where channel = 'paid_social'
  and cohort_month = '2026-07-01'
f2.label: Paid social retention, July

f3.desc: August retention minus July retention, as a share of July retention
f3.label: Change in paid social retention, August vs July

f4.desc: Paid social's retention rank among the channels in August 2026
f4.sql:
select retention_rank
from v1
where channel = 'paid_social'
  and cohort_month = '2026-08-01'
f4.label: Paid social's retention rank among channels, August

f5.desc: Paid social's August new customers as a share of all channels' August new customers
f5.sql:
select customer_share
from (
    select
        channel,
        new_customers / sum(new_customers) over () as customer_share
    from v2
) as shares
where channel = 'paid_social'
f5.label: Paid social share of August new customers

f6.desc: The channel with the highest retention in August 2026
f6.sql:
select channel
from v2
order by retention desc
limit 1
f6.label: Channel with the highest August retention

f7.sql:
select target_retention
from x1
where channel = 'paid_social'
f7.label: Paid social retention target, August

i2.text: Paid social 30-day retention rose to 46.6% in August from July's 41.7%, a relative gain of 11.8%, and ranked #1 of the four channels.

i3.text: Paid social brought in 31.2% of August's new customers, so its gain lifts retention across the whole base, not just one corner of it.

i4.text: Paid social's gain is likely to hold into September.
